caption:
This is what my family called “Tasty Rice” 🥢✨Cooking My Roots Episode 5

I swear every Chinese family has their own version of this but this one is mine. The kind of meal my mom would make, everything tossed into one rice cooker, and somehow it always hit every time.

It’s simple, comforting, and full of flavour… and yes, I always went back for seconds.

If you grew up eating something like this, you already know 🤍
And if you didn’t, you need to try it.

Rice Cooker “Tasty Rice”

Ingredients (serves 4)

2 cups jasmine rice (rinsed)
2 cups water (or chicken broth)
2–3 Chinese sausages (lap cheung), sliced
2 boneless chicken thighs, chopped
4–5 shiitake mushrooms (fresh or rehydrated dried), sliced

Marinade:
2 tbsp soy sauce
1 tsp dark soy sauce
1 tbsp oyster sauce
1 tsp sesame oil
1 tsp sugar
½ tsp white pepper
2 tsp cornstarch
Splash of water 

To serve:

Scallions, chopped
Sweet soy sauce (optional drizzle)

Instructions:
1. Rinse rice and add to your rice cooker with water or broth.
2. In a bowl, mix chicken, sausage, and mushrooms with all marinade ingredients.
3. Add the marinated mixture directly on top of the rice — do not mix.
4. Close the lid and cook as you normally would. (The meat cooks together with the rice.)
5. Once done, fluff everything together.
6. Top with scallions and a drizzle of sweet soy sauce.

That’s it. One pot, no stress, and SO good.

caption:
#ad One of the first treats that made Canada feel comforting to me as a child was Werther’s Original 🤍

So for my summer hosting dessert, I turned that same nostalgic flavour into a No-Bake Lemon Werther’s Caramel Cheesecake layered with creamy lemon filling and melted Werther’s caramel throughout.

It’s bright, refreshing, easy to make, and perfect for summer get-togethers ☀️🍋

🍋 No-Bake Lemon Werther's Caramel Cheesecake

INGREDIENTS

Crust:
• 2 cups graham cracker crumbs (or similar cookie crumbs)
• 6 tbsp melted butter

Werther's Caramel:
• 30 Werther's Original Soft Chewy Caramels
• 1/3 cup heavy cream
• Pinch of flaky salt

Filling:
• 3 blocks cream cheese, softened
• 1 cup whipping cream
• 1/3 cup icing sugar
• Juice of 1 lemon
• Zest of 1 lemon
• 3/4 of prepared Werther's caramel (reserve the remaining caramel for topping)

METHOD

1. Combine graham cracker crumbs and melted butter. Press into a 9-inch springform pan and chill.

2. Melt Werther's Original Soft Chewy Caramels with heavy cream and a pinch of flaky salt until smooth. Let cool slightly.

3. Beat cream cheese and icing sugar until roughly combined. Add lemon juice, lemon zest and half of the 3/4 of the prepared Werther's caramel and beat until smooth.

4. Add whipping cream and continue mixing until fully combined and creamy.

5. Fold in remaining 3/4 of caramel creating subtle swirls in the filling. 

6. Pour filling into the prepared crust and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight for best results. 

7. Before serving, drizzle with the reserved Werther's caramel and smooth across the top.

8. Garnish with lemon slices.

Save this recipe for your next summer get-together ☀️🍋

This honey soy chicken wings + rice cooker recipe is my follow-up to the “tasty rice” that so many of you loved… and honestly, it might be even better.

Sweet, savoury, sticky wings that soaks up all the flavour, this is the kind of meal I grew up eating and still crave.

Recipe (serves ~2–3):

Ingredients:

1–1.5 lbs chicken wings 
½ onion, sliced
½ apple, sliced

Sauce:
2 tbsp dark soy sauce
2 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tbsp oyster sauce
1 tbsp honey (+ more for brushing)
1 tbsp brown sugar
1 tsp oil

Instructions:
Add onions and apples to the bottom of your rice cooker.
Place chicken wings on top.
Pour in all sauce ingredients and mix everything together.
Let marinate for ~1 hour.

Cook using your rice cooker (about 20–30 mins, depending on your model).
Optional: Brush wings with extra honey and broil 3–5 mins for crispy skin.
Drizzle remaining sauce over everything and serve.

You can braise this in a pot if you don't have a rice cooker or you can even use the same method as my previous recipe and cook the wings with the rice!

Cooking My Roots Episode 7: Chinese Tomato Egg

#AD Growing up in a Chinese household, dinner was never just about food. 

It was how we connected.

Meals were always shared family-style, with dishes placed in the center of the table for everyone to enjoy together. And one dish I always come back to is tomato egg. It’s simple, comforting, and deeply nostalgic for me.

Looking back now, I realize how many life lessons were quietly taught during those dinners. Using serving utensils first. Making sure everyone had food before taking more. Sitting down together at the table.

At the time, they felt like small routines. But now I understand they were teaching me patience, consideration, and connection.

This Asian Heritage Month, I wanted to reflect on how food and home continue to shape the way I gather with my own family today.

Tomato Egg Recipe 🍅🍳

Ingredients:

• 4 eggs
• 2 stalks green onions, chopped
• 4 medium ripe tomatoes, chopped
• 1 clove garlic, minced
• 2 tbsp light soy sauce 
• 1 tbsp sugar
• 1 tsp white pepper
• 2 tbsp ketchup
• 1 tbsp oyster sauce
• 1/3 cup water

Instructions:

Whisk eggs and scramble in a wok over medium heat until just set, then remove.
Sauté garlic and green onions until fragrant. Add tomatoes and cook until softened.
Stir in soy sauce, sugar, ketchup, oyster sauce, and water. Simmer for 2–3 minutes.
Add eggs back in and gently mix until coated in the sauce.
Serve hot over rice ✨

✨ Crispy Air Fryer Chow Mein ✨

Welcome back to Cooking My Roots!

One of my favourite ways to eat chow mein! The air fryer makes those crispy noodles so easy, and you can top them with whatever protein and veggies you have on hand.

Ingredients

- 1 package fresh chow mein noodles
- 1 tbsp oil
- Leftover protein (I used flank steak)
- Onion & mushrooms (or any veggies)

Sauce

- 2 tbsp oyster sauce
- 1 tbsp soy sauce
- 1 tbsp brown sugar 
- 1 tsp dark soy sauce
- 1 tsp sesame oil
- dash of white pepper 
- Cornstarch slurry (1 tbsp cornstarch + 1/2 cup water)

Directions

1. Soak noodles in hot water for 2 minutes. Drain and dry well.
2. Toss with oil and air fry at 400°F for 10 minutes, flipping halfway.
3. Stir-fry your protein and veggies. Add the sauce and thicken with the slurry.
4. Spoon over the crispy noodles and enjoy!

caption:
Welcome back to Cooking My Roots (ep 4): Chinese Egg Dumplings 

This year, I’m cooking more of the Asian meals I grew up eating 🥢✨
I loved these Chinese egg dumplings growing up and they're often  enjoyed during Lunar New Year as they look like little golden nuggets, which makes them perfect for prosperity season. But for me, they taste like my mom’s kitchen and are good all year round!

I literally had to voice-note my mom and asked, “Okay wait… how did you make these?" 🥹

Here’s how:

Chinese Egg Dumplings (Sweet & Savoury)

Ingredients:
1 lb ground pork
3–4 eggs (I only use @conestoga_eggs golden yolk eggs!)
2–3 tbsp light soy sauce (divided)
2-3 tbsp dark soy sauce 
1–2 tbsp sugar
1 tbsp cornstarch
Splash of water
Handful of green onions 
Oil for frying

Step 1: In a bowl, mix ground pork with 1–2 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp cornstarch 
Step 2: Crack the eggs directly into the pork mixture, add green onions. Mix everything together really well.
Step 3: Heat oil in a pan over medium heat. Scoop spoonfuls into the pan and flatten slightly, like little omelettes.
Step 4: Fry until golden brown on both sides and cooked through. Remove and set aside.
Step 5: In a bowl, add a light & dark soy sauce, sugar, and a little water. Stir, then return everything to the pan and let them simmer until coated in that sweet and savoury glaze.

Serve on its own or over rice 🍚 Golden, comforting, protein-packed… and straight from my roots.

Lunar New Year in our home is all about blending traditions. Dumplings for prosperity, comfort food like chicken noodle soup for togetherness and @noyolkscanada Dumpling Noodles bringing it all together in this deconstructed dumpling soup. 

This recipe takes 30 minutes and one that is nostalgic to me as I remember my mom making aversion of this when we needed an easy yet nourishing meal on a busy night. A familiar bowl, reimagined for how we cook and celebrate today. #AD

Deconstructed Dumpling Soup with No Yolks Dumpling Noodles

Prep Time: 15 minutes
Cook Time: 15 minutes
Total Time: 30 minutes
Serves: 4-6

Ingredients;
Soup Base

1 bag No Yolks® Dumpling Noodles
6 cups organic chicken broth (low sodium)
½ white onion, rough chop 
2 cloves garlic, minced
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tsp sesame oil

Pork & Chicken Meatballs

1/2 lb ground pork
1/2 lb ground chicken
1 tbsp soy sauce
1 tsp sesame oil
1 tsp five spice seasoning 
1 tsp chicken bouillon powder (optional) 
1 tsp grated ginger (optional)
1 green onion, finely chopped 
1 egg yolk
1 tbsp cornstarch
Splash of water
Pinch white pepper

Vegetables
1 cup napa cabbage or baby bok choy, rough chopped
½ cup sliced carrots 

Garnish

Sliced green onions
Chili oil (optional)

Instructions
Cook noodles: 
Follow instructions on package cook and strain noodles. Set aside. 

Build broth:

In a large pot, saute onion and garlic for added aromatics. Then add chicken broth, soy sauce, sesame oil and bring to a boil.

Prepare meatballs:
In a bowl, combine pork, chicken, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger, five spice, chicken bouillon powder, green onion, egg yolk, and white pepper. Stir until paste-like texture. 

Cook meatballs:
Using a spoon, form meatballs and gently drop meatballs into simmering broth. Cook for 5–6 minutes until fully cooked.

Add noodles & vegetables:
Add No Yolks Dumpling Noodles and vegetables. Let simmer for 5 minutes until it reaches a rolling boil. 

Serve:
Ladle into bowls, garnish with green onions and chili oil if using.

One of my goals this year is to cook more meals that connect me back to my roots. I’m calling this series Cooking My Roots.

I used to think dishes like siu mai were complicated and better left to restaurants. But the more I cook the food I grew up with, the more I realize how simple, practical, and flavour-packed these meals actually are.

These homemade siu mai are: 
✔️ simple
✔️ satisfying
✔️ and surprisingly kid-approved

Not perfect. Not overly traditional. Just the kind of food I want my family to grow up with. Save this one if you’ve ever wanted to try making dumplings at home 🤍

Homemade Siu Mai (Simple + Family-Friendly)
Ingredients:
Wonton wrappers (16-18)
2 leaves Napa cabbage, finely chopped
6-7 Raw shrimp, finely chopped
1/2 lbs Ground pork
1 tbsp Garlic, minced
1 tbsp Sesame oil
2 tbsp Soy sauce
1/2 tbsp White pepper
1 tbsp Cornstarch
Splash of water
Green peas (for garnish)
Optional: caviar (because why not ✨)

Instructions:
Prep the wrappers: Trim the corners off the wonton wrappers and gently roll them out to thin slightly.

Make the filling: Finely chop napa cabbage and shrimp.
In a bowl, combine cabbage, shrimp, ground pork, garlic, sesame oil, soy sauce, white pepper, cornstarch, and a splash of water.

Mix until paste-like: Stir vigorously until the mixture becomes smooth and sticky — this is key for classic siu mai texture.

Shape the siu mai: Form a loose “C” shape with your hand.
Lay a wrapper over your fingers, spoon in the filling, and gently press down to create the siu mai shape.

Garnish: Top each dumpling with a green pea.
Steam: Line a steamer plate with napa cabbage.
Arrange siu mai on top and steam for 10 minutes, until cooked through and juicy.

Finish::Optional but extra: top with a little caviar and serve warm and don't forget a dipping sauce!

A year of denial. 
A year of planning, testing ideas, diversifying my skills, and creating income streams that didn’t rely on one title or one company.

Amplifying the voice doesn’t mean calling it quits without a plan.
It means preparing with intention. This can also be relevant to finding new opportunities within the company you work for.

Here’s what amplifying that voice actually looked like for me:
• getting curious instead of reactive
• exploring work that aligned with who I am now, not who I was a decade ago
• building flexibility before needing freedom
• separating self-worth from pay 
• trusting experience over urgency

If you’re feeling that pull right now, don’t silence it. But don’t rush it either.

One thing unemployment has taught me, one month in, is this:
I’ve spent years introducing myself by my job title… why do we do this??? When I was in my 20s, getting that fancy title meant the world to me. Even if it was made up and really didn't reflect exactly what I did. 

Somewhere in my 40s, I realized how insignificant that started to feel.

Because the truth is
👉🏽 your job title is the least interesting thing about you, especially in your 40s.
👉🏽 And losing mine made me see how deeply I had tied my identity to something that really didn't help tell me whole story. 

These past few weeks have been humbling in ways I didn’t expect:
The slow rebuilding of routine.
The space to ask: Who am I without my corporate 9-5?
Who am I when no one’s expecting anything from me?
What do I actually want for this next decade of my life?

And honestly… I’m still figuring it out but I'm getting really close to rewriting my own introduction 💪🏽

I’m learning that my worth didn’t walk out the door with my job.
I’m learning that mid-life isn’t a crisis, it’s a refresh, reset! 
I’m learning that it’s okay to want a different rhythm, a different definition of success, a different kind of life than the one I hustled for in my 20s and 30s.

If you’re in your 40s and feeling the tug to pivot, pause, or start over, please hear this:
You are not behind.
You are not early.
You are right on time for the woman you’re becoming.

This new chapter is so revealing!

Two-bite brownies @twobitebrand
Mini ice cream cones tip (CORRECTION, I meant to say @traderjoes)
White chocolate melts
Coconut oil
Sprinkles

Steps:

1. Add brownies to an electric mixer and blend until they turn into a soft, cake-like texture.

2. Roll mixture into balls sized to fit your mini cone tops. Place on a tray and chill in the fridge for 30 minutes.

3. Melt white chocolate with coconut oil in the microwave until smooth.

4. Dip each brownie ball into the melted chocolate, coat evenly, and add sprinkles. Let set.

5. Dip the rim of each cone into melted chocolate, then gently press a cake ball on top.

6. Serve and enjoy! 

No baking required! Just the way I like it!

It’s officially been one month since I became unemployed, and honestly, it’s been humbling, eye-opening, and at times challenging.
But also? A quiet gift I didn’t see coming.

Here are 7 hard truths no one really tells you about unemployment 👇

1. Your worth didn’t disappear with your job title.
I didn’t realize how much of my identity was tied to my work until I didn’t have it. I kept catching myself referring to my old company as 'us' or 'we' or reaching for my work phone that I didn't have anymore!

2. Resting isn’t lazy, it’s recovery.
That first week, I felt guilty for slowing down. I was still operating with the feeling of rush every morning even though I didn't have a set schedule anymore. Now, I’m learning that rest is part of rebuilding. I've really been enjoying long walks and not being at my desk all day! 

3. Most people you admire have been here too.
I’ve realized how many successful people have faced the same uncertainty. So many of you have shared your stories with me. With change comes new beginnings! 

4. You’ll redefine what success means. 
Without a job title, I’ve started asking: what actually feels fulfilling?
I've come to realize I want to devote my next chapter to helping founders and leaders and achieving their success! And that's exciting! 

5. You don’t owe anyone updates or rationale on your decisions.
The pressure to “have a plan” is real. But right now, showing up for yourself is enough. People will have their own POVs on your progress (or lack of) and guess what, none of that matters. Stay on your own course. 

6. One day, you’ll thank yourself for how you handled this chapter.
I can feel that future version of me cheering me on. I worked on several small side projects this month and it reminded me that the rest is still being written!! 

7. You are allowed to be happy AND unemployed!!

If you’re reading this in your own “in between” season  please remember this:
💭 You can do this! A more exciting future is ahead! And one day soon, this version of you will make total sense.
